name: process.wait
description: Wait for a process to exit. Returns its exit code. Per issue #76: `timeout_ms` is optional — when omitted, waits indefinitely until exit (or connection close, which cancels silently).

timeout_ms.description: Optional wait deadline in milliseconds. When omitted, waits indefinitely. Returns ERR timeout if the deadline expires before the process exits.

exit_code.description: Process exit code (or value passed to TerminateProcess if killed). Returns successfully even if the process had already exited before the wait began.

x-implementations.name: wait_for_multiple_objects
x-implementations.description: Win32 `OpenProcess(SYNCHRONIZE | PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION, ...)` + `WaitForMultipleObjects(hProcess, connection_cancel_event, timeout)` + `GetExitCodeProcess`. The connection-cancel event is signalled by the framing layer when the wire connection drops; the wait returns silently in that case (no response sent — the connection is gone).

windows-modern.description: OpenProcess (limited-information access) + WaitForMultipleObjects with a connection-cancel event for clean shutdown semantics. ERR not_found when OpenProcess fails (process exited and pid was recycled).

windows-classic.description: Same APIs across NT 4 / 9x onwards. NT 4 has `PROCESS_QUERY_INFORMATION` instead of `PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION` (the latter is NT 6+) — agent uses the former on classic.
